rules.title: Trait satisfaction derivation modes
rules.statement: satisfies(T, X) holds iff at least one derivation succeeds: (D) a direct impl fact impls(T,X); (B) a blanket impl blanket(T←{Tb...}) whose every bound Tb satisfies satisfies(Tb,X); (A) an auto impl auto(T) with no negative carve-out; or (S) a shape-auto impl shape_auto(T,S) whose predicate S(X) matches with no negative carve-out.

rules.title: Negative impls beat all derivations
rules.statement: A negative fact !impls(T,X) makes satisfies(T,X) false unconditionally; it is checked before and overrides direct, blanket, auto and shape-auto derivations.

rules.title: Fixed derivation priority order
rules.statement: Resolution tries derivations in strict order: negative carve-out (reject), then direct, then blanket, then auto, then shape-auto. The first kind that succeeds determines the result; later kinds are not consulted.
rules.uncertainty: Phase-1 simple priority ordering; coherence/overlap checks are stated to live elsewhere.

rules.title: Blanket impl bounds are an AND-conjunction
rules.statement: A blanket impl blanket(T←{Tb1..Tbn}) derives satisfies(T,X) only if every bound trait Tbi satisfies satisfies(Tbi,X) for the same type X. An empty bound set {} is an unconditional impl-for-all-types of T.

rules.title: First fully-satisfied blanket wins
rules.statement: When multiple blanket impls target the same trait T, the first one (in declaration/registration order) whose bounds are all satisfied is selected; remaining candidate blankets are not considered.
rules.uncertainty: Coherence is deferred; overlapping blankets are resolved by order rather than rejected here.

rules.title: Cyclic blanket bounds resolve to no-impl on the cyclic path
rules.statement: If resolving satisfies(T,X) recursively re-enters the same query (T,X) through a blanket-bound chain, that recursive path yields no impl rather than diverging, allowing outer rules to try alternatives; resolution always terminates.

rules.title: Resolution result per (trait,type) is memoized and stable
rules.statement: satisfies(T,X) is a deterministic function of the current fact set: results (including negative/no-impl outcomes) are memoized per (T,X) pair and re-queries return the same answer until the fact set changes.

rules.title: Adding a fact may flip previous negative results
rules.statement: Adding any impl fact (direct, blanket, auto, shape-auto, or negative) invalidates all previously cached resolution results, because a prior 'no impl' may become satisfiable (or vice versa).

rules.title: Duplicate direct impls collapse to one impl identity
rules.statement: Registering a direct impl for an already-implemented (T,X) pair does not create a new impl; the original impl identity is returned, so impls(T,X) names a single impl.

rules.title: Derived auto/shape impls get a fresh stable impl identity per (trait,type)
rules.statement: Auto and shape-auto derivations produce a fresh impl identity the first time a given (T,X) pair is queried; that identity is memoized so subsequent queries of the same pair compare equal.

rules.title: Shape-auto impls match by a predicate over the type name
rules.statement: A shape-auto impl applies to type X iff its shape predicate evaluates true on X's type name; a shape-auto impl with no predicate never matches.
